first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this so I read it properly on the iPad. The opening tells me straight away there's no single figure, which is a bit frustrating when I'm the one helping pay, but at least it isn't pretending. It reads sensibly and nobody's trying to be cute with me, so I kept going.

journey.quote: A single figure blends all of those together and says very little about your own wedding.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, but I'd still like some sense of scale before I tell my husband what we're in for. I understand why it isn't here, though.

journey.quote: Ask each supplier which currency the quote, deposit and balance are invoiced in, when each payment falls due and what happens to money paid if plans change.
journey.reaction: Good. This is exactly what I'd be asking. Seeing deposits right at the top tells me they've thought about people like me.

journey.quote: An overseas business selling directly to Australian consumers must follow the Australian Consumer Law, but a remedy can be difficult to obtain in practice, so read the cancellation terms before you pay.
journey.reaction: Honest, and that's the worry I have. But it leaves me asking: if a supplier over there takes the money and vanishes, who is actually on our side? The page doesn't say what Wedded Wonderland does about that.

journey.section: Season and day of the week
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months, and wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September.
journey.reaction: Useful, and it makes me think straight away of my mother in the heat. Then it moves on to shade and water and never comes back to older guests.

journey.section: The legal route and its fees
journey.quote: Documents issued abroad must be recent originals, officially translated into Greek, and those from outside the European Union need an Apostille.
journey.reaction: I'm glad it's spelled out, but this section is heavy going. Several long sentences in a row about embassies and DFAT. I had to read it twice.

journey.quote: If guests are island hopping, who carries the cost of a cancelled ferry and an extra night?
journey.reaction: Very practical, I like this list. But nothing about whether an elderly guest can manage the ferry, the steps, the cliff paths. My mother uses a walking frame. That's my first question and it isn't asked anywhere.

journey.quote: If the binding version is in Greek, ask which version prevails if the two differ, and have anything unclear read before you sign.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is the sort of thing I'd never have known to ask. That earns real trust.

journey.section: Deposits and when payments fall due
journey.quote: Ask whether the deposit secures the date, whether it is refundable, and what happens to it if you postpone.
journey.reaction: Good, but postponing isn't my fear. My fear is the supplier cancelling or closing. That should be asked here too.

journey.quote: Australia and Greece have no agreement covering medical care for tourists, so visitors pay for all medical care, including hospital stays and evacuation.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that. Important for the older relatives. I'd forward this bit to my husband.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and has inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: That is what I wanted to hear. AUD and in writing. I'd like to know who this person is, though, and whether I can talk to them on the phone.

journey.quote: What happens if a ferry is cancelled or the weather turns on the day?
journey.reaction: Good question, but the bigger one is who do we ring if something goes wrong at 2am their time. It isn't on the list.

journey.section: Planning your Greece wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, accountable, fee in writing. That's the reassurance I needed. I'd still want a phone call before anything is booked.

unanswered_questions: Can older guests or anyone with a walking frame get to the ceremony, the reception and their rooms? What should we ask venues about steps and access?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong on the day, or at 2am Greek time?
If a Greek supplier cancels or closes, what happens to the deposit, and does the Wedded Advisor help us get it back?
Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor by phone before anything is booked, and can a parent who is paying be included in those conversations?
Roughly what range should a family expect? Even a broad starting point would help me talk to my husband.
Does the Wedded Advisor's quote in AUD fix the amount, or can the euro still move it after we've agreed?

turn_offs_found.quote: The [Australian Embassy in Athens](https://greece.embassy.gov.au/athn/notarial.html) issues certificates of no impediment and applies apostilles to original Australian public documents, and a fee applies. DFAT also legalises Australian documents for a fee, with slower processing in peak holiday periods.
turn_offs_found.why: Dense run of official-sounding sentences. Not unbroken text exactly, but hard work on an iPad. I'd prefer it as a short list of steps.

turn_offs_found.quote: When a service has a [major problem](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/problem-with-a-product-or-service-you-bought/repair-replace-refund-cancel), you can cancel and get a refund, which may not be in full because you pay a reasonable amount for work already done, or keep the contract and pay a lower price.
turn_offs_found.why: One long sentence doing a lot of work. Important information, but I lost the thread.

would_share_with: My husband (the deposits, contracts and medical care sections, with my questions about access for Mum)
My daughter, to ask whether she has spoken to a Wedded Advisor yet

cta_reaction.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: One accountable person and a fee in writing is exactly right for me. I'd click if it said I could talk to someone on the phone, and if the page had shown it understood older guests and what happens to deposits if a supplier lets us down. As it stands I'd more likely send it to my husband first and let my daughter make the enquiry.

top_3_changes:
Add an access question for older or less mobile guests to the transfers list. old: "- If guests are island hopping, who carries the cost of a cancelled ferry and an extra night?" new: "- If guests are island hopping, who carries the cost of a cancelled ferry and an extra night?
- Can older guests, or anyone with limited mobility, get to the ceremony, reception and their rooms, and is there a route without steep steps?"

Ask who to contact out of hours in the planner questions. old: "- What happens if a ferry is cancelled or the weather turns on the day?" new: "- What happens if a ferry is cancelled or the weather turns on the day?
- Who is our contact if something goes wrong during the trip, and how do we reach them out of hours?"

Cover the supplier letting you down, not just postponing. old: "Ask whether the deposit secures the date, whether it is refundable, and what happens to it if you postpone." new: "Ask whether the deposit secures the date, whether it is refundable, and what happens to it if you postpone or the supplier cancels or stops trading."

open_questions.question: Mobility and accessibility for older guests is absent from the whole draft; is this a gap the writer should close with questions only, given no sourced facts?
